extracted.intended_audience: Recommenders for the Hertz Fellowship (faculty, mentors, supervisors, industry references)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for people asked to complete the Hertz Fellowship recommender/reference form, describing submission process, required form components, and the evaluation criteria used to assess applicants' potential for innovative research in the applied physical sciences and engineering.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommender form submission deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: All recommender forms must be submitted by Monday, November 3, 2025 at 6:00 pm Pacific.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 2026 Hertz Fellowship application will open on August 28, 2025 and close on October 31, 2025. Recommender forms have a fixed submission deadline (Nov 3, 2025). Contact fellowshipinfo@hertzfoundation.org with questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Method of submission — use the reference form (no letters)
rubrics_metrics.description: No. We learn more about our applicants through our specific form questions rather than a standard letter. This form also contains checkbox questions up front which are important for our review process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Once an applicant identifies you as a recommender in their application, it will trigger an email notification requesting that you complete a reference form. Do not submit a traditional letter of recommendation in place of the form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess degree of fundamental knowledge in the applicant's field
rubrics_metrics.description: For the rubric, we ask you to assess the applicant on several dimensions, including their degree of fundamental knowledge in their field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate how well the applicant understands core principles of their discipline (especially physical principles). Your assessment will inform their preparedness for high-level, innovative research rather than judging specific proposals only.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess self-reliance and independence in scientific work
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess the applicant's self-reliance and independence in scientific work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comment on evidence that the applicant can plan and carry out research independently, make decisions without excessive supervision, and demonstrate initiative in conducting scientific work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess possession of fertile imagination
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess the applicant's possession of fertile imagination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider the applicant's capacity for creative thought, idea generation, and envisioning novel approaches to problems; provide examples if possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess originality in the applicant's work
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess the applicant's originality in their work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate how the applicant's work departs from standard approaches, adds new perspectives, or demonstrates novel contributions, with concrete instances preferred.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide brief examples of creativity, initiative, and problem-solving
rubrics_metrics.description: For the short questions, we are seeking insights into what makes this individual truly stand out. You will be asked to briefly discuss meaningful examples of the applicant’s creativity, initiative and problem-solving abilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give concise, meaningful anecdotes or instances that illustrate these traits rather than general praise. Emphasize actions, outcomes, and context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Describe instances of confronting real-world challenges or applied research
rubrics_metrics.description: We are particularly interested in instances where the applicant has confronted real-world challenges or engaged in research within the applied physical sciences and engineering.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highlight examples where the applicant applied scientific knowledge to practical problems or real-world settings, including collaborations with industry, translational projects, or engineering-focused research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess applicant relative to peers at a similar stage
rubrics_metrics.description: You will be asked to assess the applicant in comparison to their peers at a similar stage of education, with a focus on identifying their key strengths and potential.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a comparative judgment (e.g., top 1%, top 10%, among top X) and explain which strengths or capabilities justify that placement. Focus on potential for exceptional innovation rather than on a single project’s merit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reflect on potential biases to support fair and equitable review
rubrics_metrics.description: As you complete the evaluation, we encourage you to reflect carefully on any potential biases and consider how you can contribute to a fair and equitable review process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be mindful of conscious or unconscious biases in assessments. Where relevant, contextualize achievements relative to opportunities and provide equitable comparisons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form workflow and technical requirements (Save/Print/Submit)
rubrics_metrics.description: If you need to finish the form at a later time, simply click “Save for Later” at the bottom of the form. You can PRINT or SAVE a copy of your completed form but must do so BEFORE SUBMITTING IT.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the Preview button and the print icon on the next screen to print or save a PDF of your completed form prior to submission. Before submitting, review carefully to ensure correct information and that nothing is autofilled incorrectly.
